sections.html:
Caroline County is in eastern Virginia, with the Rappahannock River along its north edge. Richmond is about 30 miles to the south and Fredericksburg 32 miles to the north, so many residents drive out for work along Interstate 95, which crosses the county at exits 104 and 110. The county covers 537 square miles and had 30,887 residents in 2020. The seat and largest town is Bowling Green; the only other incorporated town is Port Royal.

Many homes are fairly recent additions to an older farming area, because the population is roughly double what it was fifty years earlier. The commute is the first thing buyers ask about, and a house near an I-95 exit is simpler to pitch than one at the end of a long rural road.

Caroline sets two real estate due dates, June 5 and December 5. The day after each, on June 6 and December 6, the county tacks on a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest, and the same applies to personal property and business personal property.

Bill or feeDue date
First installmentJune 5
Second installmentDecember 5
Penalty and interest10 percent each, added the next day
Water bills15 days from the billing date
Dog tagJanuary 31
Business licenseMarch 1

The state sets the ceiling in Code of Virginia 58.1-3916, which allows a locality to charge up to 10 percent a year interest plus a penalty of up to 10 percent on past-due property tax. Both can be waived if the taxpayer was not at fault, or if the payment went out on time with proof of mailing and arrived within five days of the deadline.

sections.h2: Treasurer and Commissioner of the Revenue contacts
sections.html:
One office collects and another assesses. The Treasurer takes payment, and the Commissioner of the Revenue handles assessment questions.

  • Treasurer: 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, VA 22427. Mail goes to P.O. Box 431. Phone 804-633-5291, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Real estate questions at the Commissioner's office: 804-633-9834 or realestate@co.caroline.va.us.
  • General county mail: P.O. Box 447, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

You can pay online, by phone through ACI, by mail, at the counter or through monthly automatic withdrawal, and a drop box outside the County Administration Building takes payments after hours. The county stands behind only payments made through its own website and Official Payments. If you use your own bank's bill-pay service, any delay is on you.

sections.h2: How to check or appeal your assessment
sections.html:
Begin on the county's Real Estate Assessment Information tool at caroline.civ.quest and its Tax Map page, then phone the Commissioner's real estate office. Still unhappy after a reassessment? The Board of Equalization is next.

The order runs like this. First come hearings with the Board of Assessors. Then a Board of Equalization takes complaints: six citizens, nominated by the Board of Supervisors and approved by a Circuit Court judge in every general reassessment year, each trained by the Virginia Department of Taxation. Once that board is done, a petition to the Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984 is all that remains.

Know the burden before you file. Section 58.1-3379 treats the assessor's figure as correct, and the owner has to show it exceeds fair market value, was applied unevenly, or ignored accepted appraisal practice. On a residence with fewer than four units, a written request for the assessment records must be answered within 15 days.

sections.h2: Permits, land use and utilities before you sell
sections.html:
Permits, land use, utilities and deed costs are the local items that touch a sale. Each has its own office, and each is worth a phone call early.

  • Building permits: any new building, renovation, addition or major improvement needs a permit, plus plumbing and mechanical permits. A certificate of occupancy follows satisfactory completion. Building Inspections is at 804-633-4303. Sort out unpermitted work before you list.
  • Land use: the Commissioner of the Revenue runs the land preservation program and rechecks each enrolled property every year. Ask that office whether your parcel is enrolled and what rollback would apply.
  • Utilities: the county names the Carmel Church Ladysmith, Milford, Port Royal and Townfield water systems. Public Utilities is at 804-633-4390.
  • Relief for older and disabled owners: call the real estate office at 804-633-9834.

At closing, the grantor tax under Virginia 58.1-802 is fifty cents on every $500 of value. The statute names the seller as payer, though the two sides can agree to split it differently.

Owing back taxes means piled-up penalty and interest and a larger payoff when you close. The county adds both charges the morning after each due date, so a missed December 5 bill starts growing immediately.

Request the balance for your expected closing day from the Treasurer, then have the closing agent verify it. If the house needs more repair than a retail buyer would tolerate, a cash purchase in present condition saves fix-up and showing time, and the unpaid balance is paid out of the sale money.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Caroline County house with back taxes and work from whatever number the Treasurer hands you.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the two due dates
sections.html:
Listing in spring puts the June 5 bill close to closing, and listing in fall puts December 5 there. Ask the closing agent whether the current installment is paid and who covers the days of the year each side owned the house. A bill due the week of closing is the most common source of last-minute questions.

If you miss a due date while a sale is pending, the penalty and interest land the next day, so it is cheaper to pay on time and settle the split at closing than to wait. The Treasurer can tell you the exact amount for the day you plan to close, and a written figure is easier for everyone to work from than a phone estimate.

1. Phone the Treasurer, 804-633-5291, and ask what is owed on each installment.
  2. Search caroline.civ.quest for your parcel and see whether the record fits the house.
  3. Raise land use or relief with the real estate office, 804-633-9834.
  4. Make sure every permit has been closed out through Building Inspections.
  5. Give the closing agent a written payoff and your receipts.

None of these steps takes long. Done a few weeks before listing, they head off the late surprises that tend to stall a Caroline sale, such as an open permit, an unpaid water bill or a payoff nobody has confirmed. Heirs selling from out of town should start with the Treasurer's call, since a balance can be larger than expected once penalty and interest are added.

faqs.q: When are Caroline County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments fall on June 5 and December 5. Miss one and the county adds penalty and interest, 10 percent each, the following day.

faqs.q: Where is the Caroline County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: Walk in at 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, on weekdays between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., or call 804-633-5291. Letters go to P.O. Box 431, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Caroline County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: Begin with the real estate office run by the Commissioner of the Revenue. If that fails, take the dispute to the Board of Equalization, and then to Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Caroline County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The unpaid balance is taken out of your proceeds at the closing table, so get a fresh payoff figure from the Treasurer and let the closing agent double-check it.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax when a Caroline County house sells?
faqs.a: By statute the seller owes it, at fifty cents per $500. A buyer can agree to cover part or all of the amount.
